name: UCI Student Performance Dataset (Math)
citation: Cortez, P., & Silva, A. (2008). Using data mining to predict secondary school student performance. In Proceedings of 5th Annual Future Business Technology Conference (FUBUTEC 2008), pp. 5-12, Porto, Portugal.
target_definition: Binary risk indicator where 1 = at-risk (final grade G3 < 10 on a 0-20 scale) and 0 = passing (G3 >= 10).

target_leakage_policy.rationale: G3 is the source of the target label and must never be in X. G2 is a late-stage term-2 grade, excluded to ensure predictions represent an early-warning signal.

uci_dataset_schema: Demographics/Social: school, sex, age, address, famsize, Pstatus, Medu, Fedu, Mjob, Fjob, reason, guardian

Academic/Behavioral: traveltime, studytime (1-4 categorical scale), failures (past failed classes 0-4), schoolsup, famsup, paid, activities, nursery, higher, internet, romantic, famrel, freetime, goout, Dalc, Walc, health, absences (total missed classes 0-93)
Assessment grades: G1 (term 1 score 0-20), G2 (term 2 score 0-20), G3 (final score 0-20)
feature_mismatch_documentation.domain_gap_analysis: The UCI benchmark reflects Portuguese secondary school education with detailed familial, behavioral, and absence count variables, whereas the current application schema captures college-level engineering metrics (USN, branch, percentage attendance, 10-point GPA scale, backlogs). Features are NOT silently substituted. The ML pipeline is trained on genuine UCI benchmark data with full feature traceability.

evaluation_methodology: Stratified 80/20 train/test split with fixed random seed (42). Feature preprocessing fitted strictly on training fold via Scikit-learn ColumnTransformer. Both models fitted with class_weight='balanced' to address ~2:1 class imbalance. Final evaluation computed on holdout test set using Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, and Confusion Matrix.
